input: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

business.claim: Sells a business-to-business platform covering global payroll, HR, benefits, immigration, performance management and device management, serving startups through enterprises.
Its employer-of-record service lets customers employ workers internationally without establishing their own local entities; Deel handles employment contracts, payroll, benefits and compliance.
As_of 2026-11-10, advertised recurring fees start at $49 per contractor per month and $599 per employer-of-record employee per month; these are starting prices, not all-in customer costs.
Company claim: supports global employment operations across 150 countries as_of 2026-11-10.
Third-party research provider Sacra describes additional monetization through foreign-exchange spreads and payment infrastructure, alongside recurring platform fees.
Company claim: its contractor stablecoin wallet was available in 80+ countries across Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific as_of the page's 2026-11-09 update.

traction.claim: Company claim: more than 40,000 customers as_of 2026-11-10; the public page does not define active, paying or contracted customer status.
Company claim: named customers include Robinhood and Revolut; its homepage features a Robinhood finance-executive endorsement and a Revolut case study.
Company claim: processed $22 billion in payroll annually and served more than 1.5 million workers as_of its October 2025 financing announcement; payroll throughput is not Deel revenue.
Company claim: revenue run rate reached $800 million as_of December 2024, with 70% year-over-year growth.
Partner confirmation: Stripe announced Deel's stablecoin-wallet launch on 2026-06-03, using Stripe payments, Bridge issuance, Privy wallets and Tempo settlement. Initial availability was Argentina.

Company claim conveyed through an executive interview: an October 2026 podcast featuring SVP of Product Aaron Goldsmid attributes more than $140 million in ARR to AI optimization. The podcast description is not independently audited evidence of incremental sales.

team.claim: Founded in 2019 by Alex Bouaziz and Shuo Wang. As_of 2026-11-10, Deel identifies Bouaziz as CEO and Wang as Chief Revenue Officer.
Company biographies state that Bouaziz previously co-founded Sarona Ventures, while Wang co-founded Aeris Cleantec and served as its CTO before its acquisition by iRobot.
Joe Kauffman is President and CFO as_of 2026-11-10. His company biography identifies prior CEO, President and CFO roles at Credit Karma.
Deel announced Kauffman's appointment on 2025-11-03; former CFO Philippe Bouaziz remained Executive Chairman and Chief Strategy Officer. This was a role transition, not a company departure.
Dan Westgarth is COO as_of 2026-11-10; his company biography states that he previously held senior leadership roles at Revolut.
The current leadership page lists Yaron Lavi as CTO, Harish Sharma as Chief Risk Officer, Anthony Rodriguez as Chief Compliance Officer and DeAnn Work as Global Corporate General Counsel.
The federal court's description of the parties identifies Philippe Bouaziz as CEO Alex Bouaziz's father.

Notable departure within the review window: Bloomberg reported on 2025-04-04 that communications chief Elisabeth Diana had resigned the preceding week. She previously led Instagram communications and was a Facebook vice president.

funding.claim: As_of May 2020: $14 million Series A; lead: Andreessen Horowitz.
As_of 2020-09-09: $30 million Series B; lead: Spark Capital.
As_of 2021-04-21, Globes reported a $156 million Series C at a $1.25 billion post-money valuation, co-led by YC Continuity, Andreessen Horowitz and Spark Capital.
As_of 2021-10-18, raised a $425 million Series D led by Coatue at a $5.5 billion valuation.
As_of 2022-05-11: Axios reported $50 million raised at a $12 billion valuation; Emerson Collective joined.
As_of 2025-02-04: reported $300 million secondary sale to General Catalyst and Mubadala at $12.6 billion; not primary financing.

Company claim: October 2025 Series E raised $300 million at a $17.3 billion valuation, co-led by Ribbit Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. This is the latest priced primary round verified for this memo.
Company claim: the press page still quotes a $17.3 billion valuation as_of 2026-11-10; this is not an executable secondary-market price.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim: revenue has exceeded $1.5 billion as_of 2026-11-10. The press page does not specify the measurement period or explicitly label this figure ARR.
Third-party estimate: Sacra estimates $1.5 billion in annualized revenue as_of June 2026, versus $1.3 billion at year-end 2025. These are annualized estimates, not audited full-year revenue.
Company claim: September 2025 was its first $100 million revenue month and marked three consecutive years of profitability; the announcement does not provide audited earnings or cash-flow statements.
Historical headcount comparator, company claim: nearly 7,000 team members as_of 2025-06-02.

Current headcount disclosure, company claim: more than 7,000 team members as_of 2026-11-10. Compared with the historical disclosure, these rounded figures do not establish a precise organic headcount growth rate.
Hiring signal: the company careers page displayed 238 open positions as_of 2026-11-10, including 95 in Sales, 32 in Payroll and 11 in Engineering. Listings do not establish net hiring.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In People Center v. Deel, the court allowed core civil RICO and trade-secret allegations concerning alleged corporate espionage to proceed on 2026-02-23. This was a pleading-stage ruling, not a finding that Deel committed the alleged conduct.

On 2026-09-25, the court denied Deel's effort to strike the central witness's affidavit, compelled arbitration of certain computer-access counterclaims, stayed Deel's RICO counterclaims and dismissed some other counterclaims while allowing some false-advertising allegations to proceed.
Company position: Deel denies Rippling's allegations and says its federal counterclaims allege anticompetitive conduct and deceptive business practices by Rippling.

The Wall Street Journal reported a DOJ criminal investigation and grand-jury subpoenas concerning the alleged spying scheme as_of 2026-01-24. Deel said it was unaware of a criminal investigation and would cooperate; this report is not a charging document.

A court-approved agreement dated 2026-05-21 required Deel to reimburse $66,062.25 of Rippling's legal fees and Rippling to withdraw its sanctions motion, following a tentative finding of some sanctionable discovery misconduct. It was a stipulated resolution, not a final adjudication of all misconduct allegations.

In Damian v. Deel, the receiver alleged deficient AML, sanctions and licensing controls. The court dismissed the action for standing and RICO-enterprise pleading deficiencies on 2025-08-18; dismissal did not adjudicate whether the alleged compliance failures occurred.

Company-confirmed security incident: unauthorized access to CRM information was confirmed on 2026-06-17 through a compromised Klue integration. Business-contact and commercial data, plus limited personal data, were affected; Deel says its platform itself was not involved and that vendor access was revoked.

Latest discovery development located: an automated legal-summary publisher reports a 2026-11-06 order requiring forensic data from Alex and Philippe Bouaziz's phones by 2026-11-12 unless stayed. This secondary account was opened; the underlying order was not independently retrieved.

Product disclosure, not an enforcement finding: Deel states that DLUSD balances are not bank deposits or legal tender, lack FDIC or equivalent insurance, and offer variable, non-guaranteed promotional rewards.

reputation.claim: Employee-review platform snapshot: Glassdoor displayed 4.3/5 from 2,147 reviews as_of 2026-11-10. This is user-generated review data, not a verified employee-satisfaction survey.

Recent Glassdoor reviews are mixed: November 2026 entries praise compensation and remote flexibility, while others complain about limited ownership, delivery pressure and management's AI-adoption demands. The opened snapshot does not establish a longitudinal ratings trend.

Customer-review platform snapshot: Trustpilot displayed 4.5/5 from 9,760 reviews as_of 2026-11-10. The profile identifies a paid subscription and says Deel invites reviews; neither fact establishes review manipulation.

Trustpilot's AI-generated review summary is broadly positive on usability, transfers and onboarding, but identifies complaints about delayed bonuses or expenses, support tracking and international payroll compliance. Individual visible reviews also describe compliance-review holds; allegations are not independently verified.

Critical press: Bloomberg characterized the September 2026 court rulings as setbacks for Deel, reporting the rejected witness challenge and counterclaim limitations. Deel declined comment for that article.

red_flags.claim: Investment inference from the litigation above: surviving civil RICO and trade-secret claims create material legal and management-distraction risk, although liability has not been established.
The reported criminal probe elevates diligence beyond ordinary commercial litigation; current investigation status remains unverified.
The discovery-fee settlement and preceding tentative misconduct finding warrant review of document preservation and litigation controls.

The confirmed CRM compromise demonstrates third-party integration risk. Deel's statement that its platform was unaffected should not substitute for reviewing the incident report, affected-data inventory and remediation evidence.

Revenue disclosure requires reconciliation: the current press page uses an unspecified revenue measure. Do not treat that statement as audited trailing annual revenue or automatically equate it with ARR.

Stablecoin balances introduce an additional diligence area: Deel expressly disclaims deposit insurance and guaranteed rewards. Review partner responsibilities, redemption arrangements and customer disclosures before underwriting this product.

output.verdict: As_of 2026-11-10, Deel's reported customer scale, repeated institutional financing and experienced finance leadership support continued diligence. Investment approval should depend on reconciling revenue and cash-flow quality, reviewing client-money and third-party security controls, and obtaining counsel's assessment of the civil litigation and reported criminal investigation.

cost_basis: tokens x list price + $10 per 1K web search calls
